# Make the data of your health research speak {.page-title}

[Every health topic has data that can tell a story: what is known, who works on it, who funds it, and where the gaps are. We help in two ways: **we teach researchers to do it themselves**, and **we deliver clear evidence for organizations that need to act**. Infectious and non-infectious diseases alike.]{.lead}

[For researchers and students]{.eyebrow}

## Learn to do it yourself

[You know your topic better than anyone. We help you turn that knowledge into a dataset, a dashboard and an article, and you keep the skills. Every session works on your own topic. No coding experience needed. In French or English.]{.lead}
:::

::: {#discovery .work-item .reveal}
[3 hours · online · group]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Discovery workshop

A first, practical look at what the data on your topic can show.

- The open sources you can use: OpenAlex, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, funding and patent data
- How to turn a health problem into a clear data question
- Real examples from health research

[Result: a clear plan for your own topic]{.tag .tag-amber}

[See the public workshops](workshops.qmd)
:::
:::

::: {#bootcamp .work-item .reveal}
[4 weeks · 8 live sessions · small group]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Bootcamp: make your topic's data speak

From the first day, you work on your own topic, step by step, with a small group of peers.

- Build a literature and funding corpus on your topic
- Use Python or R in Google Colab, from zero
- Use AI and large language models for screening and extraction, with human checking
- Build a simple dashboard and write up your results

[Result: your own dataset, a dashboard and a draft article]{.tag .tag-amber}
:::
:::

::: {#coaching .work-item .reveal}
[One-to-one · 6 to 8 weeks]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Build together: coaching on your project

We work side by side on your real project: a review, a grant application, a thesis chapter or a new study. You learn by doing, and you finish with a real output.

[Result: a finished output and new skills]{.tag .tag-amber}
:::
:::

::: {#teams .work-item .reveal}
[2 to 3 days · online or on site]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Training for teams and labs

Your whole team learns one shared method, adapted to your field, so you can repeat the work on every new project.

[Result: a team that can do it again]{.tag .tag-amber}
:::
:::

:::
:::

[What you learn]{.eyebrow}

## Four levels, from first steps to advanced

[Every level uses health examples from infectious diseases (such as Marburg virus, antimicrobial resistance and phage therapy) and non-infectious diseases (such as cancer, diabetes and mental health).]{.lead}
:::

::: {.grid .grid-2}
::: {.card-cx .reveal}
[Level 1]{.card-num}

### Foundations

- Turn a health problem into a data question
- Open sources: OpenAlex, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, funding and patents, Global Burden of Disease
- Build a good search strategy, with no-code tools
:::

::: {.card-cx .reveal}
[Level 2]{.card-num}

### Build

- Python or R in Google Colab
- Collect data through APIs and clean it
- Screen and extract with AI, and check the results
:::

::: {.card-cx .reveal}
[Level 3]{.card-num}

### Communicate

- Charts and dashboards (Quarto, Tableau Public)
- Write articles and policy briefs
- Publish an open dataset with a DOI (Zenodo)
:::

::: {.card-cx .reveal}
[Level 4]{.card-num}

### Advanced

- Collaboration networks and topic modelling
- Equity analysis: funding, gender, geography
- Patent analysis
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.band}
::: {.wrap}
::: {#organizations .section-head}
[For NGOs, health programs, funders and institutions]{.eyebrow}

## Clear evidence, delivered

[You need to understand a health topic quickly, without technical detail. We do the work and give you results you can read, share and act on.]{.lead}
:::

::: {#snapshot .work-item .reveal}
[About 2 weeks]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Evidence snapshot

A short brief with key charts that answers one clear question. For example: *Who is researching and funding this disease in our region, and what is missing?*

[Result: a 2-page brief, the charts and the data]{.tag .tag-amber}
:::
:::

::: {#landscape .work-item .reveal}
[4 to 6 weeks]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Landscape report

A complete picture of a health topic from publications, funding, trials and patents: research trends, main actors, collaborations, gaps and equity (countries, gender, neglected areas).

[Result: a report, an open dataset and an interactive dashboard]{.tag .tag-amber}

**Examples:** our [patent landscape of phage therapy](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-024-02493-9), published in *Nature Biotechnology* (2024), and our [Marburg virus equity explorer](dashboards/marburg-equity.qmd).
:::
:::

::: {#dashboard .work-item .reveal}
[Setup, then regular updates]{.work-meta}

::: {}
### Living dashboard

An online observatory for your topic, updated regularly, so your team and partners always have current evidence.

[Result: a dashboard that stays up to date]{.tag .tag-amber}
:::
:::

:::
:::

## A simple process

[Each project gets a clear proposal with a fixed price, agreed before we start. Prices are adapted to your country's income level.]{.lead}
:::

::: {.grid .grid-4 .steps}
::: {.step .reveal}
[Step 1]{.card-num}

### A free call

20 minutes on your topic and your goal.
:::

::: {.step .reveal}
[Step 2]{.card-num}

### A one-page proposal

Within 48 hours: scope, timeline, deliverables and a fixed price.
:::

::: {.step .reveal}
[Step 3]{.card-num}

### A mid-point review

You see the work in progress, so there are no surprises.
:::

::: {.step .reveal}
[Step 4]{.card-num}

### Delivery and handover

You receive the results and we walk you through them. For training, a certificate.
:::
